mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior month reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified rate hike period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) create a dual pressure that depresses corporate earnings growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases over the same month
regime_hint: labor market softening with weak consumer demand
failure_condition: IC rank > 0.05 over 60-day window or 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified interaction period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 5% in a month signals accelerating supply-side momentum that outpaces consumer absorption, prompting excess optimism in growth expectations and a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or INDPRO growth is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) below 11,000 billion chained dollars for three consecutive quarters suggests structural supply constraints, which lowers future earnings expectations and yields a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or GDPC1 recovers above 11,000B in the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in three months, it typically coincides with central bank easing, which reduces the real interest rate and supports equity valuations, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% after a 3-month decline
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) or UNRATE does not fall below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 jobs in a single month creates a strong labor market signal that boosts investor confidence in corporate earnings, generating a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or payroll growth is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price indexes (CPIAUCSL) above 2% indicate accelerating inflation expectations that force the Federal Reserve to maintain higher policy rates, which compresses equity discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month growth > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative or inflation decelerates rapidly.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential housing starts (not available in the provided catalog) would be a classic supply-side shock, but as this series is unavailable, we instead posit that a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 for two consecutive months signals supply chain disruptions that lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month falls below 105 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or INDPRO recovers above 105 within the next quarter.
